target_customer: Men with spinal cord injury or disease who need long term bladder drainage, via urologists and rehabilitation clinicians
problem: People with neurogenic bladder rely on repeated intermittent catheterization or external indwelling catheters that carry infection and injury risks; the Connected Catheter is a fully internal indwelling device.
business_model: Medical device sales after regulatory clearance, funded meanwhile by equity and non-dilutive grants

founders.name: Derek Herrera
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a medical device entrepreneur and CTO. A trade press summary says he is a former Marine special operations officer paralyzed in Afghanistan; not verified from an opened page.

founders.name: Zach McKinney
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page; no bio.

technical_complexity.rationale: An implanted internal indwelling urethral device needs biocompatibility, device engineering, clinical trials and FDA pathway work for a very small team.

defensibility.rationale: Regulatory clearance and clinical data would be hard to copy, but the product remained investigational so the moat was unproven.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copying shown. A 2024 trial record for the catheter was marked terminated and no acquirer was found.

market_need_then: Guidance from spinal cord injury sources lists intermittent catheterization or indwelling urethral or suprapubic catheters as standard options, all with infection and injury risk (undated clinical guidance). Dated 2016 demand figures were not found.

branding.name_origin: Spinal Singularity: not explained by sources. UroDev Medical renaming in February 2021 per press release: Herrera said the company had evolved and wanted a name reflecting that growth, broadening beyond spinal injury.
branding.domain_note: Site urodevmedical.com returned HTTP 503 when fetched.

rebrands.why: Company had evolved and wanted to broaden device use beyond spinal injury patients, per press release coverage

brand_strength.rationale: Mission story in press, but small brand with a rename and no consumer awareness data.

outcome_analysis: Spinal Singularity entered YC in Winter 2016 to develop the Connected Catheter, raised a 3.1M dollar seed in October 2017 and secured NIH and Defense related grants, then renamed itself UroDev Medical in February 2021 with a new CEO and a move to Minnesota. YC lists it as acquired but no acquirer or date was found, and a 2024 clinical study record is marked terminated. The cause and form of the exit are not public in the sources found.
notes: Seed confirmed by BioSpace and MassDevice. Grants (NIH Phase II SBIR about 1.5M, DoD awards reported over 3.6M for FY18, earlier NIH and NSF about 0.5M) are reported in search results without dates, so they are not recorded as rounds. Acquisition status per YC only; Trelleborg appears in a search result about the Connected Catheter but no source states an acquisition so it is not recorded. Business Wire release returned 403 so rename details come from BioSpace summary. No dated 2016 competitor source found.
